title: Factor Code Networks
authors: Abhisek Sahu, Jeremy van der Heijden, Mark Van Raamsdonk, Rana Zibakhsh
abstract: For a quantum code defined by an isometry $T:H_{\rm code} \to H_{\rm phys}$, an operator map is a *-homomorphism $\varphi: B(H_{\rm code}) \to B(H_{\rm phys})$ from the space of operators on the logical Hilbert space to the space of operators on the physical Hilbert space satisfying $\varphi({\cal O}) T = T {\cal O}$ for every operator ${\cal O}$ on $H_{\rm code}$. This can additionally be taken to be unital $\varphi(I_{code}) = I_{phys}$ if and only if $\dim H_{\rm code}$ divides $\dim H_{\rm phys}$. In this case, $\varphi(B(H_{\rm code})$ is a von Neumann factor subalgebra of $B(H_{\rm phys})$ and we call the pair $(T,\varphi)$ a {\it factor code}.   A code network is a family of Hilbert spaces $\{{\cal H}_i\}$ indexed by a partially ordered set with isometries $T_{ji}:{\cal H}_i \to {\cal H}_j$ for $i < j$ satisfying $T_{kj} T_{ji} = T_{ki}$ for $i < j < k$. In this paper, we ask when this can be promoted to a {\it factor code network} by defining unital operator maps $\varphi_{ji}$ so that $(T_{ji}, \varphi_{ji})$ is a factor code and $\varphi_{kj} \varphi_{ji} = \varphi_{ki}$. We show that the divisibility conditions on Hilbert space dimensions are sufficient for any code network with a tree structure but not in general. For a diamond-shaped network, we show that promotion is possible if and only if the principle angles between $T_{42} H_2$ and $T_{43} H_3$ all have multiplicity divisible by $H_1$.   For incomparable $i_1,i_2 < j$, we characterize when $\varphi_{j i_1} (B(H_{i_1}))$ and $\varphi_{j i_2} (B(H_{i_2}))$ commute, when they generate all of $B(H_j)$, and when they intersect only on multiples of the identity. For $i < j_1,j_2 < k$, we characterize when $\varphi_{k j_1} (B(H_{j_1})) \cap \varphi_{k j_2} (B(H_{j_2})) = \varphi_{k i} (B(H_{i}))$ and when these algebras together with $B(H_k)$ form a nondegenerate commuting square.
summary: This paper develops the mathematical theory of 'factor code networks,' generalizing quantum error-correcting codes to structured networks. It determines the precise algebraic and geometric conditions—such as dimension divisibility or specific angle multiplicities—required for these networks to be consistently defined by compatible operator maps. This work is crucial for understanding the structure of quantum information encoded across complex, hierarchical physical systems.
main_problem: The paper characterizes the conditions under which a general quantum code network, defined by isometries on a partially ordered set, can be promoted to a consistent 'factor code network' via compatible unital operator maps.
main_result: Promotion is possible for tree structures if dimension divisibility holds, but for more complex geometries like diamond networks, it requires specific geometric conditions related to the multiplicities of principal angles between subspaces.
method: The authors use abstract algebra, von Neumann algebras, and geometric analysis involving principal angles to establish necessary and sufficient conditions for the existence of the required commuting operator maps.
model_or_system: The model is a quantum code network, which generalizes quantum error-correcting codes by indexing the structure over a partially ordered set. The core mathematical objects are isometries $T_{ji}$ and the associated operator maps $\varphi_{ji}$.
key_observables: Principal angles between subspaces ($T_{42}H_2$ and $T_{43}H_3$), and the algebraic structure of the generated von Neumann factor subalgebras ($\mathcal{M}$).
important_parameters: The ratio of Hilbert space dimensions ($\dim H_{	ext{phys}} / \dim H_{	ext{code}}$) must be an integer for a factor code.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes finite-dimensional Hilbert spaces, allowing the use of matrix algebra and von Neumann factor theory.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate Hasse diagrams for code networks, showing examples of structures that either satisfy or fail the promotion criteria, particularly for diamond-shaped networks.
paper_structure: The paper first defines factor codes and code networks, then develops characterizations for the maps ($\varphi$). It proceeds by analyzing specific network topologies: tree structures, diamond-shaped networks, and general conditions for commuting/intersecting subalgebras.
why_interesting: The rigorous mathematical framework developed for factor code networks provides powerful tools for analyzing tensor network structures arising in quantum gravity or quantum field theory, linking algebraic consistency to geometric constraints.
